html:
Divide decimals without changing the quotient

Division asks how many divisor-sized groups fit into the dividend, including a fractional group when the question allows it. Multiplying both numbers by the same nonzero power of ten preserves this quotient.

Make the divisor a whole number before using long division. Preserve all the digits of the dividend. Append zeros if more decimal places are needed; do not round the dividend to make the work easier.

A method to try

  1. Multiply both dividend and divisor by the same power of ten until the divisor is whole.
  2. Divide from left to right, recording zeros in the quotient when needed.
  3. Continue into decimal places when required and check quotient times divisor.

Worked examples

12.74 ÷ 2.45

Multiply both numbers by 100: 1274 ÷ 245. Five groups use 1225, leaving 49; 49/245 is 0.2.

12.74 ÷ 2.45 = 5.2

Check: 2.45 × 5.2 = 12.74.

14.375 ÷ 1

Dividing by one leaves the original value unchanged. All three decimal places remain.

14.375 ÷ 1 = 14.375

Check: 14.375 × 1 = 14.375.

A mistake to watch for

Changing only one number changes the quotient. Rounding 14.375 to 14.38 changes the problem.

Check and explain

Check using exact multiplication, not rounded values.
